3. Validate unsafe code with Miri using non-Copy drop-tracking types.

For most real Rust projects, the bounded queue is the better first primitive: simpler memory management, stronger
cache locality, easier validation, and fewer reclamation hazards. The unbounded queue is useful when backpressure is
not acceptable, but it carries much more complexity because reclamation correctness becomes part of the algorithm.
